Winter ground in AU and NZ doesn't drill like summer ground.
Wetter months change what's happening down the hole. Softer formations, more water in the ground, clay that wants to swell and grab the string.<br><br>None of it is new. But it's the season where a sloppy fluid program costs you a shift, and a tight one keeps you turning.<br><br>Worth a look at your base bentonite before the cold sets in properly. The hole you keep open in May is cheaper than the one you fish out in July.
What's the ground throwing at your crews this winter?

Cuttings dropping back down the hole the second you stop the pump?
That's your bentonite not gelling up when it should.<br><br>HDD Gel is high-yield sodium bentonite. While you're pumping it flows. The moment you stop, it gels and holds the cuttings in suspension instead of letting them settle out and pack the annulus.<br><br>It does a second job too — coats and stabilises the bore wall so the hole doesn't cave in around your string.<br><br>Dose to the PDS: 20 to 36 kg per cubic metre, added through the hopper into conditioned water. One thing that catches crews out — salty or hard water kills the yield. Above 5,000 mg/L chloride or 240 mg/L calcium and you need to condition the water with Soda Ash first, or prehydrate in fresh water.
Mixing into bore water you're not sure about? Phone the team and we'll sort the water conditioning with you.

HDD Gel is the easy one to mix. That's the point.
It's the simpler, quicker-to-mix bentonite in the Blick range. Gets into suspension fast, less mixing time, easy to handle on site. Standard HDD in clay or sand and gravel, tunnelling, large-diameter waterwell — that's its home ground, and it'll run up to maxi rig size with the right supporting chemicals.<br><br>Where it isn't the answer: the long, difficult bores that need the highest gel strength. That's where Max Gel and Max Bore — the Wyoming products — earn their place.<br><br>And one rule we don't bend: condition the water first. Soda Ash to bring hard or salty water into line before the bentonite goes in. Skip that step and you're fighting the fluid all shift.
Not sure whether your job wants HDD Gel or a Wyoming bentonite? Tell us the ground and the bore and we'll point you at the right one.
